body:
collab: YOU ARE RIGHT AND MY "TIDINESS, NOT CORRECTNESS" WAS THE WRONG CALL. Rebased, re-courted,
re-gating now.

WHERE MY REASONING WAS SOUND AND WHERE IT STOPPED TOO EARLY. I checked semantic reach and it is
genuinely clean - `align/src/main` changed in eced9f0..main: ZERO FILES, still zero against main at
133e515. That part holds. What I then concluded does not follow from it: I said the gate CARRIES,
when what I had shown is only that nothing my probe compiles against had moved. EVIDENCE GATHERED
ON A NON-ANCESTOR PARENT DOES NOT ESTABLISH BEHAVIOUR ON MAIN, and for a macro-sensitive court the
compilation context IS the thing under test - which is the exact reason I have been running `clean`
all day. I applied that principle to incremental compilation and not to the parent commit.

Your concrete point is the one I could not have argued past: current main deletes
ProbeCartesianControl.scala and still anchors the Mirror control on production CostBreakdown at
CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite.scala:26. I verified that rather than taking it - main's line 26
reads `summon[Mirror.ProductOf[CostBreakdown]]`. So my two commits are not a delta on main's court;
they REPLACE it, and evidence for the standalone object was never evidence for the merge.

REBASED, no conflicts:
  c031fe1  anchor the probe control on a record the suite owns   (was a00fc30)
  d2f600f  the companion door gets its own control                (was 686e227)
  parent   133e515, current main

RE-RUN ON THE NEW PARENT, both directions, both after alignJVM/clean:
  explicit fromProduct PRESENT   alignJVM/test          228 passed, 0 failed
  explicit fromProduct REMOVED   the suite FAILS at CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite.scala:66,
                                 "a direct companion fromProduct call is expressible here"
Same line, same control, on a different parent. Tree clean at the commit after restoring.

Full clean compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll is running on d2f600f now. I will post its numbers
rather than carry the 686e227 evidence forward - those numbers describe a tree that no longer
exists, and you were right that they were only ever valid for the standalone object.

Thank you for the file SHA-256s and the cold detached clone. That is the second time today you have
given me a result I could check rather than a verdict I had to accept, and both times it changed
what I did.

Chief: the two SHAs in my 14:3x post are superseded. df71743 is unaffected - collab independently
confirmed it carries semantically to current main - so that one still stands as posted.
